title: CNNs: LeNet to ResNet Shape Reasoning

questions.question: After the first valid 5x5 convolution in lenet_shape_trace((1,1,32,32)), what is the tensor shape?
questions.explanation: A valid 5x5 operation removes four pixels from each spatial dimension and uses six output channels in the LeNet trace.

questions.question: Why is the LeNet flatten entry (1, 400) for the default trace?
options: The first convolution has 400 filters
The second pool leaves 16 channels at 5x5, so 16*5*5 = 400
The input has 400 pixels after converting RGB to grayscale
The class count is multiplied by the batch size
questions.explanation: The trace has `(1,16,5,5)` after the second average pool; flattening multiplies only those channel and spatial dimensions.

questions.question: What does residual_add require before adding a main and shortcut branch?
options: Only matching heights; channels may differ
Matching batch size but any spatial size
Matching complete NCHW shapes
A scalar shortcut so broadcasting can choose the channels
questions.explanation: Elementwise addition is defined only when N, C, H, and W match in this local contract; a real projection must change a mismatched shortcut first.

questions.question: What does avg_pool2d(x, kernel=2) do to a (1,1,4,4) input with its default stride?
options: Returns (1,1,4,4) by padding every border
Returns (1,2,2,2) by treating pooling as a channel split
Returns a scalar average over the whole image
Returns (1,1,2,2) with each value the mean of a non-overlapping 2x2 window
questions.explanation: The default stride equals the kernel, so valid non-overlapping windows halve both spatial dimensions while retaining channels.

questions.question: If num_classes changes from 10 to 7, which part of model_parameter_counts changes?
options: Only the final dense layer's output terms (84*classes + classes)
Every convolutional kernel because classes changes input channels
The 16*5*5 flatten width
The batch dimension in every trace entry
questions.explanation: The feature extractor and hidden dense widths stay fixed; only the final 84-to-class weight and bias terms depend on the class count.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes this lesson's relationship to LeNet, VGG, and ResNet?
options: It downloads the historical LeNet weights and reproduces their test accuracy
It checks local NumPy shapes and formulas; it is not a pretrained or fully trainable framework checkpoint
It implements batch normalization and residual training exactly as a modern ResNet
It replaces all convolution with dense layers to avoid spatial contracts
questions.explanation: The code deliberately exposes shape/value primitives so the architecture decisions remain testable even without Torch or external weights.
